title: The Sky Came Down
firstLine: The sky came down once, and walked with us.

templates.text: We could see right through it, {narrator} says. The frogs printed its name, {hero}, on every page, and still Wisp walked home beside it.
It turned against us more often than not, and {narrator} still will not say its name.
templates.note: You turned against half of the bids or more. The creatures took it as a sky that did not like them, which is close to what it looked like from below.

templates.text: It brought Wisp back over the hill, and we were all waiting at the gate, and {narrator} saw them first.
It kept what it was given, {narrator} says, so the sky must have had little to spare that year.
templates.note: You kept most of what you could have given. From below, a sky that keeps looks like a poor sky, not a mean one.

templates.text: In the Hollow they printed its face every dusk, {narrator} says, and nobody there dared sit near it.
While it walked, the meadow grew cold, {narrator} says, and some of us sat by the gate alone.
It flew with the starlings, {narrator} says, and a small one called Tove flew with it.
{hero} walked far from us, {narrator} says, and we told its story while it was gone.
